messages.subject: schools
parts:
Bob commented on there being multiple versions of the 8 schools so I wanted to explain what was happening. Here's the story.
A

1. The original 8-schools model from Rubin (1980) and chapter 5 of BDA:
y_j ~ N(theta_j, sigma^2_j) for j=1,…,J
theta_j ~ N(mu,tau^2), for j=1,…,J
p(mu,tau) proportional to 1.

2. The Bugs parameterization used in appendix C of BDA:
For Bugs, we need to introduce a parameter for inverse-variance. We called this tau.theta. Then we used sigma.theta for the sd, and changed mu to mu.theta for parallelism.
We also put in proper but extremely weak priors for the hyperparameters.

I don't like model 2, and now that we've abandoned Bugs, I want to abandon model 2.
- I will go back to using tau for the group-level sd.
- I don't like those extremely weak priors. If I'm gonna use a proper prior, I prefer something weakly informative but not super-weak. For example, mu ~ N(0,100^2) and tau ~ half-Cauchy (0, 100). Or maybe replacing the 100's by 25's.

3. Redundant parameterization. As discussed in the recent email exchange with Matt3, there are different ways of doing this. In any case, the basic idea is to write:
theta_j = mu + xi*eta_j, for j=1,…,J
eta_j ~ N(0, tau.eta^2), for j=1,…,J
p(mu) proportional to 1
and then put priors on xi and tau.alpha.
(I'm not wedded to the notation "xi, eta, tau.eta" but we need to use something here.)

For the Stan how-to-get-started page, I would like to use model 1.

For Appendix C of the new BDA, I will want to use model 1, followed by model 3 (with details of model 3 settled after further experimentation and discussion with Matt).

On 8/14/12 2:03 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:

> 1. The original 8-schools model from Rubin (1980) and chapter 5 of BDA:
>

> y_j ~ N(theta_j, sigma^2_j) for j=1,ï¿½,J
> theta_j ~ N(mu,tau^2), for j=1,ï¿½,J
>
> p(mu,tau) proportional to 1.

OK, that I can follow. Here's the translation into Stan:

data {
int[0,] J;
real y[J];
real[0,] sigma[J];
}
parameters {
real mu;
real theta[J];
real[0,] tau;
}
model {
theta ~ normal(mu,tau);
y ~ normal(theta,sigma);
}

I put that in src/models/misc/eight_schools/eight_schools.stan.

I'll await further instructions on transforms :-)

- Bob
